title: Optical vortex bullets with large angular momenta
authors: José R. Salgueiro, Carlos F. Sánchez, Boris A. Malomed, Ángel Paredes, Humberto Michinel
abstract: We investigate three-dimensional spatiotemporal optical vortex solitons (light bullets with a toroidal shape) carrying higher-order orbital angular momentum in Kerr media with anomalous group-velocity dispersion and a transversely localized Gaussian profile of the linear refractive index. Stationary vortex bullets with topological charges (winding numbers) $1\leq \ell \leq 4$ are obtained as numerical solutions of the three-dimensional nonlinear Schrödinger equation, and their existence, structure and stability are systematically analyzed. In terms of atomic Bose-Einstein condensates, these solutions represent matter-wave solitons with embedded vorticity. We examine the dependence of the solution families on the propagation constant, the depth and width of the guiding profile, and $\ell $. It is found that the increase of $\ell $ requires one to use a stronger or wider waveguiding potential to sustain localized states satisfying the Vakhitov-Kolokolov (VK) stability criterion. VK-complying and non-complying branches of vortex-soliton families are separated by a degenerate Townes branch. Direct simulations reveal that, although the guiding profile substantially suppresses the collapse and extends the propagation distance of vortex bullets, their robustness is ultimately limited by azimuthal instabilities, whose growth is enhanced for values of $\ell $. These results demonstrate that engineered refractive-index landscapes significantly enlarge the stability domain of spatiotemporal vortex bullets and provide guidelines for supporting optical bullets carrying large orbital angular momenta.
summary: This work theoretically analyzes stable, high-angular-momentum optical vortex solitons propagating in structured nonlinear media. By modeling the system using the nonlinear Schrödinger equation, the authors demonstrate that while engineered guiding potentials enhance stability, the structures remain susceptible to azimuthal instabilities. The findings provide crucial guidelines for controlling and supporting complex quantum light/matter waves.
main_problem: The study investigates the existence, structure, and stability of three-dimensional spatiotemporal optical vortex solitons (light bullets) carrying high orbital angular momentum.
main_result: Engineered refractive-index landscapes significantly enlarge the stability domain for these vortex bullets, although their robustness is ultimately limited by azimuthal instabilities that grow with angular momentum.
method: The analysis involves solving the (3+1)D nonlinear Schrödinger equation numerically, using stability criteria like the Vakhitov-Kolokolov (VK) criterion.
model_or_system: The system models light propagation in Kerr media with anomalous group-velocity dispersion and a transversely localized Gaussian refractive index profile. This is mathematically analogous to matter-wave solitons in Bose-Einstein condensates.
key_observables: Topological charge ($\ell$), Norm ($N$), Field amplitude evolution over propagation distance ($z$), and Instability growth rate.
important_parameters: Topological charge ($\ell=1$ to $4$), Guiding potential strength ($\gamma$), and Guiding profile width ($q$).
main_assumptions: The stability analysis relies on the Vakhitov-Kolokolov (VK) criterion, which is necessary but not sufficient for full stability.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate vortex bullet cross-sections, the dependence of the norm on the propagation constant ($ eta$) relative to the VK criterion, and the growth of azimuthal instability as a function of $\ell$ and $\gamma$.
paper_structure: The paper systematically analyzes the solutions to the reduced nonlinear Schrödinger equation, first establishing the existence of stable states based on the VK criterion, and then using direct simulations to probe the ultimate limitations imposed by azimuthal instabilities.
why_interesting: The direct analogy to matter-wave solitons in BECs makes this highly relevant to AMO physics, providing theoretical guidelines for stabilizing complex, high-angular-momentum quantum matter waves.
